title: fastpath: gating and safe-mode fallback for precision-toggle KV-cache + batching
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: The fastpath codepath provides substantial latency improvements for common request shapes (short sequences, cached KV layouts, and standard precision), but has historically caused correctness regressions when internal assumptions about KV layout or numeric precision are violated. This PR introduces a conservative gating mechanism and a runtime "safe-mode" fallback that forces the slower, general path when divergence is detected. Goals: 1) Preserve the observed tail-latency and throughput improvements for healthy workloads. 2) Eliminate correctness regressions caused by rare precision mismatch / KV-cache corner cases. 3) Add observability and controls so operators can tune aggressiveness per deployment. Summary of changes: - Fastpath gating: Add pre-execution checks that validate KV-cache layout (shape/version tags) and dtype/quantization metadata before entering the fastpath. If a validation fails, the request is routed to the general (slow) path. - Safe-mode fallback: Introduce a rolling-window detector that watches for model output divergence or runtime exceptions. When the error rate or divergence metric exceeds configurable thresholds, the node flips into safe-mode for a configurable cooldown period and serves all requests via the general path. - Precision toggle handling: Make precision-toggle APIs idempotent across cached KV states. On precision transition (e.g., FP16 -> BF16 or quantized), the node will either rebuild KV cache or invalidate cached entries used by fastpath checks. - Continuous batching scheduler changes: Update the scheduler to prefer batching on fastpath-capable requests but keep a low-latency single-request lane for requests that fail gating checks. Adds an adaptive timer to avoid batching-induced tail spikes when safe-mode is active. - Kernel and execution changes: A small refactor in the kernel selector to expose the "compatible-with-fastpath" predicate. No functional change for general kernels; this is used only for routing. - Observability: New metrics and traces: fastpath_attempts, fastpath_successes, fastpath_reasons (list of enumerated failure reasons), safe_mode_activations, kv_invalidations, precision_transitions. Added a dashboard for tracking fastpath health and rollout impact. - Config / operator controls: new config flags under runtime.fastpath.*: enabled (bool), gating_thresholds (json-string in config), safe_mode.enabled, cooldown_secs, min_requests_window. - Tests: unit tests for gating predicates, integration tests that simulate precision toggles and KV cache mismatches, end-to-end perf benches. Rollout plan: feature gated off by default in main. Enable in staging for 48h with aggressive tracing; then progressive canary rollout to 5% of production traffic. If safe-mode flips more than 0.5% of requests in canary, abort and revert. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~10% median and 15% p95 improvement for workloads that hit fastpath; safe-mode introduces negligible overhead when inactive (~<1% throughput loss). In pathological edge-cases we observed fastpath rejections ~0.4% of requests, and the fallback path increases per-request cost by ~8% for those requests. Implementation notes: - Key parts of gating check added in runtime/request_router.cc and runtime/fastpath_guard.h - Safe-mode state machine implemented in runtime/safe_mode_manager.{cc,h} - Scheduler changes in runtime/scheduler.cc (small scheduling policy edits + adaptive timer) - Config and metrics in runtime/metrics_registry.cc Test-plan: - Unit tests added under tests/unit/fastpath_test.cc - Integration tests under tests/integration/safe_mode_end_to_end.cc that replay production traces with synthetic precision toggles - Performance job added to CI bench pipeline; local perf runs attached in comment History / related: This PR builds on the earlier work in ENG-2308 (fastpath kernel selection) and ENG-2471 (KV cache consistency fixes). Also addresses hotfixes from incident INC-2026-02-05 where an FP16/quantized model rollout caused unexpected token divergence. Checklist: - [x] Add gating checks and tests - [x] Implement safe-mode detector and cooldown - [x] Integrate metrics and dashboard - [x] Add operator controls and docs - [x] Run perf benches and validate improvements - [x] Add integration tests and CI bench job

discussion: Liam Patel (reviewer) 2026-02-11: Can we make the gating checks cheap? We should avoid extra allocations on the hot path.
Ava Chen (author) 2026-02-11: The gating checks are O(1) metadata inspections and use existing cache-version fields; added microbench to show <200ns median overhead when fastpath is active.
Sofia Martinez (reviewer) 2026-02-12: Safe-mode cooldown default feels conservative. Suggest 60s -> 30s for canary to reduce blast radius.
Ava Chen 2026-02-12: Reduced default cooldown to 30s for canary; kept configuration so operators can set longer in prod.
Noah Brooks (approver) 2026-02-16: Verified integration test against replayed traces; metrics look sane. Approving.

Release lead 2026-02-17: Added note to release notes about safe-mode default being off and rollout recommendations.
release_notes: Introduce conservative fastpath gating + safe-mode fallback to prevent correctness regressions when KV cache or precision changes occur. Default fastpath is disabled in main; enable via runtime.fastpath.enabled. Adds observability and operator controls. No breaking API changes.
perf_summary: ~10% median and ~15% p95 improvement for fastpath-capable workloads observed in staging perf runs. Fastpath rejection rate observed ~0.4% in replayed traces; fallback cost ~+8% on those requests. Overall system throughput improved ~6-9% in typical traffic mixes.
